_comment: Copy this to skills/<your-skill>/evals/evals.json and replace the cases.
Delete this _comment block and the `note` fields once you are done.
A dataset is two lists of prompts. `expected_matches` are the ones that
should wake your skill up; `expected_no_matches` are the ones where no
skill should fire at all. Nothing names a skill: the folder says which
skill this is, and the list a prompt sits in says whether it triggers.
Write prompts the way a user would actually type them -- copying phrases
out of your SKILL.md description measures string matching, not routing.
If a prompt should trigger a DIFFERENT skill, put it in that skill's
`expected_matches`, not in your `expected_no_matches`. Routing installs
the whole catalog at once, so it is the same assertion either way, and
your list keeps meaning 'nothing should fire'.
Tier 0 (required for every skill): at least 3 `expected_matches` and 2
`expected_no_matches`.
Tier 1 (required if your skill can be exercised on a generic runner): give
at least one case a `should` / `should_not` / `logs_contain` / `files_exist`
expectation, so something grades what the skill did and not just whether it
fired.
Tier 2 (hardware or a live service): add skills/<your-skill>/evals/machine.yml
so CI knows where to run it. Most skills do not need one.
Check your work without spending tokens:
python eval/run_evals.py --validate
Then run it for real:
python eval/run_evals.py --skill <your-skill>

expected_matches.prompt: Something a user would say that should make this skill fire.
A different phrasing of the same need, with none of the same keywords.

expected_matches.note: Tier 1. The same prompt grades routing AND what the agent then did.
expected_matches.prompt: A task this skill should carry out end to end.
should: A thing the agent must do, in plain language, graded by an LLM judge
should_not: A mistake this skill exists to prevent

expected_no_matches.note: Close to this skill's vocabulary but out of its scope: the wrong hardware, an adjacent domain, a question rather than a task.
expected_no_matches.prompt: Something that sounds like this skill's territory but is not.
Another prompt that must not wake this skill up.
